source.title: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry
source.copyright_handling: Facts are paraphrased into original source records; no long textbook passages are copied.

pipeline_notes.intended_use: Generate visual-first micro-problem flashcards for the organic chemistry explorer.
pipeline_notes.schema_note: This worktree did not contain the referenced ochem schema, so this file is self-contained and section-scoped.
pipeline_notes.avoid_simple_deck_duplication: The existing Organic Chemistry I deck already covers broad prefix and functional-group recall. These records emphasize richer structure recognition, naming decisions, and conformational reasoning.

learning_goals: Recognize common organic functional groups from patterns and examples.
Classify alkanes as saturated hydrocarbons and use CnH2n+2 for acyclic alkanes.
Distinguish constitutional isomers from alternate drawings of the same compound.
Name straight-chain and branched alkanes using parent chains, locants, substituents, and suffixes.
Recognize alkyl groups and classify carbons and hydrogens as primary, secondary, tertiary, or quaternary where applicable.
Relate alkane physical properties to molecular size, branching, and dispersion forces.
Interpret sawhorse and Newman projections for ethane, propane, butane, and substituted alkanes.
Compare staggered, eclipsed, anti, and gauche conformations using torsional and steric strain.

global_visual_requirements.purpose: Render line-bond, condensed, and partially expanded structures for naming and isomer recognition.
requirements: Support straight-chain, branched-chain, and substituent-highlighted alkane structures.
Allow atom or bond highlighting for parent-chain selection, branch points, and functional groups.
Include optional condensed formula labels only when the card asks for formula reasoning.

global_visual_requirements.purpose: Show free rotation around sigma bonds and let learners inspect conformers.
requirements: Provide an axis marker for the C-C bond being viewed.
Support front/back carbon coloring that matches Newman projections.
Expose dihedral angle readout in degrees for conformation cards.

global_visual_requirements.purpose: Generate Newman projections from a chosen viewing bond.
requirements: Draw front-carbon bonds to the center and rear-carbon bonds to the circle edge.
Support staggered, eclipsed, anti, and gauche placements.
Allow substituent labels such as H, CH3, Cl, Br, Et, and generic R.

global_visual_requirements.purpose: Plot relative potential energy versus dihedral angle.
requirements: Mark staggered minima and eclipsed maxima.
Support quantitative annotations in kJ/mol and kcal/mol.

global_visual_requirements.purpose: Render named alkyl substituents and their attachment points.
requirements: Mark the free valence or attachment atom clearly.
Include common and systematic names where both are useful.
Differentiate primary, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary carbon environments visually.

global_visual_requirements.purpose: Render generic functional group patterns and concrete molecule examples.
requirements: Use R groups for generic patterns and real atoms for examples.
Highlight the atoms defining the functional group.
Support multiple functional groups in one molecule without ambiguous colors.

facts.statement: A functional group is a recurring atom pattern inside a molecule that largely determines a family of chemical behavior.
Molecules with the same functional group often react in related ways even when the rest of the molecule is very different.
Alkenes contain a carbon-carbon double bond; alkynes contain a carbon-carbon triple bond; arenes contain aromatic carbon-carbon bonding in a ring.
Alkyl halides, alcohols, ethers, phosphates, amines, thiols, sulfides, and disulfides feature carbon singly bonded to an electronegative atom.
A carbonyl group is a C=O unit. Aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, esters, thioesters, amides, acid chlorides, and anhydrides differ by what is attached to the carbonyl carbon.
In carbonyl groups, the carbonyl carbon is electron-poor relative to the oxygen, making the C=O bond strongly polarized.

candidate_cards.prompt: Highlight the functional group in a molecule containing both an alkene and an alcohol.
candidate_cards.answer: Identify C=C as alkene and R-OH as alcohol.

candidate_cards.prompt: Choose whether the C=O compound is an aldehyde, ketone, ester, amide, or carboxylic acid.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Classify by the atoms attached to the carbonyl carbon.

candidate_cards.prompt: What functional group is represented by R-C#N?
Given a line structure, list every functional group present without naming the whole molecule.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Return all highlighted group families and ignore alkyl skeleton details unless asked.

facts.statement: Acyclic alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons: they contain only carbon and hydrogen and only single C-C and C-H bonds.
Acyclic alkanes follow the general formula CnH2n+2.
Methane, ethane, and propane each have only one carbon skeleton; formulas C4H10 and larger can have multiple constitutional isomers.
Straight-chain alkanes have all carbons connected in one unbranched row; branched-chain alkanes contain side branches from the longest chain.
Constitutional isomers have the same molecular formula but different atom connectivity.
The number of alkane constitutional isomers grows rapidly with carbon count: C6H14 has 5, C7H16 has 9, C8H18 has 18, C9H20 has 35, and C10H22 has 75.
Different drawings can represent the same alkane when atom connectivity is unchanged; rotation and drawing orientation do not create constitutional isomers.

candidate_cards.prompt: Does C7H16 fit the formula for an acyclic alkane?
candidate_cards.answer: Yes. For n = 7, CnH2n+2 gives C7H16.

candidate_cards.prompt: Decide whether two drawings of C4H10 show the same connectivity or constitutional isomers.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Butane and 2-methylpropane are constitutional isomers; rotated or bent drawings of n-butane are the same compound.

candidate_cards.prompt: How many constitutional isomers does C6H14 have?
Given two condensed formulas and two line drawings, group representations that show the same alkane.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Compare atom connectivity, not drawing direction or chain bending.

facts.statement: An alkyl group is the substituent fragment obtained conceptually by removing one hydrogen from an alkane.
Alkyl group names usually replace the parent alkane ending -ane with -yl.
R is a generic symbol for an unspecified organic group, often read as the rest of the molecule.
A primary carbon is bonded to one other carbon; secondary to two; tertiary to three; quaternary to four.
Hydrogens are classified by the type of carbon they are attached to; there is no quaternary hydrogen because a quaternary carbon has no C-H bond.
The prefixes sec- and tert- describe attachment through secondary and tertiary carbons in common alkyl group names.

candidate_cards.prompt: Name the alkyl group formed by removing one H from methane.
Classify the highlighted carbon as primary, secondary, tertiary, or quaternary.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Count directly attached carbon atoms, not hydrogens.

candidate_cards.prompt: Classify the highlighted H atoms as primary, secondary, or tertiary.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Use the class of the carbon bearing each hydrogen.

candidate_cards.prompt: Match isopropyl, sec-butyl, isobutyl, and tert-butyl to structures with marked attachment points.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Use the attachment carbon and branching pattern.

sections.title: Naming Alkanes

facts.statement: An IUPAC alkane name combines a parent chain, substituent prefixes, locants, and the -ane suffix.
The parent hydrocarbon is the longest continuous carbon chain; the drawn zigzag may need to be followed around corners.
If two chains of equal length are possible, choose the chain with more branch points as the parent.
Number the parent chain from the end that gives the first branch the lower locant; if tied, compare the next branch point.
Every substituent receives a locant; two substituents on the same carbon receive the same locant.
Use di-, tri-, tetra-, and related prefixes for repeated identical substituents, but ignore those multiplier prefixes when alphabetizing.
Use commas between numbers and hyphens between numbers and words; the final alkane name is written as one word.
A branched substituent can be named as its own substituent, numbered from the attachment point, and placed in parentheses in the full molecule name.
Common substituent names such as isopropyl, isobutyl, sec-butyl, and tert-butyl are accepted in many contexts.
For alphabetizing common substituents, iso is treated as part of the name; sec- and tert- are not.

naming_algorithm: Find the longest continuous carbon chain and assign the corresponding alkane parent name.
If equal-length parent chains are possible, select the one with more substituents.
Number from the end nearer the first substituent; use the next point of difference if the first comparison ties.
Name each substituent and assign its locant.
Use multipliers for repeated substituents and include one locant per substituent.
Alphabetize substituent names, ignoring di-, tri-, tetra-, sec-, and tert-, but counting iso.
Write the final name as one word, with commas between locants and hyphens between locants and words.
For a branched substituent, number it from the attachment point and put its name in parentheses.

candidate_cards.prompt: Select the correct parent chain in a branched alkane where the longest path turns a corner.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Choose the longest continuous carbon chain, not the longest horizontal segment.

candidate_cards.prompt: Give the IUPAC name for a highlighted branched alkane.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Apply parent-chain selection, numbering, substituent naming, alphabetizing, and punctuation.

candidate_cards.prompt: Draw 4-ethyl-2,2-dimethylhexane.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Start from hexane, place two methyl groups at C2, place ethyl at C4, then verify carbon valence.

candidate_cards.prompt: Explain why a proposed alkane name violates IUPAC rules.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Check longest parent chain, lowest locants, alphabetizing, and substituent naming.

candidate_cards.prompt: Name a molecule containing a 2-methylpropyl substituent on a longer parent chain.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Name the branched substituent from its attachment point and place it in parentheses if using systematic substituent form.

facts.statement: Alkanes are often chemically inert toward many laboratory reagents and are sometimes called paraffins.
Alkanes can burn in oxygen to form carbon dioxide and water while releasing substantial heat.
Methane can undergo chlorine substitution under ultraviolet light to give chlorinated methane products.
Straight-chain alkane boiling and melting points generally rise as carbon count and molecular weight rise because dispersion forces increase.
More highly branched alkane isomers usually boil lower than less branched isomers because compact shapes have less surface contact and weaker dispersion attractions.

property_comparisons.reason: Branching makes the molecules more compact and reduces dispersion-force contact.
The branched isomer has lower surface area.

candidate_cards.prompt: Which should boil higher: pentane or octane?
candidate_cards.answer: Octane, because the larger molecule has stronger dispersion forces.

candidate_cards.prompt: Rank pentane, isopentane, and neopentane by boiling point.
Complete the combustion products of an alkane.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Combustion of a hydrocarbon gives CO2 and H2O when oxygen is sufficient.

facts.statement: Stereochemistry studies the three-dimensional arrangement of atoms in molecules.
Rotation around an open-chain carbon-carbon sigma bond is possible because sigma bonds are cylindrically symmetric.
Conformations are different spatial arrangements produced by rotation around single bonds; conformers often interconvert rapidly.
A sawhorse representation views a C-C bond at an oblique angle; a Newman projection views directly down the C-C bond axis.
In a Newman projection, bonds on the front carbon meet at the center, while bonds on the rear carbon attach to the edge of the circle.
Ethane's staggered conformation places C-H bonds as far apart as possible and is lower in energy than the eclipsed conformation.
Ethane's eclipsed conformation is about 12 kJ/mol (2.9 kcal/mol) higher in energy than staggered ethane.
The extra energy of an eclipsed conformation is torsional strain; in ethane, each H/H eclipsing interaction contributes about 4.0 kJ/mol (1.0 kcal/mol).
A dihedral angle describes the angle between bonds on adjacent atoms when viewed along the bond connecting them.

candidate_cards.prompt: Identify whether a Newman projection of ethane is staggered or eclipsed.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Staggered bonds alternate around the circle; eclipsed bonds line up front-to-back.

candidate_cards.prompt: Label the front and rear carbon substituents in a Newman projection.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Front-carbon bonds meet at the center; rear-carbon bonds start from the circle.

candidate_cards.prompt: Which ethane conformer is lower in energy, staggered or eclipsed, and by about how much?
candidate_cards.answer: Staggered ethane is lower by about 12 kJ/mol (2.9 kcal/mol).

candidate_cards.prompt: On an ethane rotation-energy diagram, identify maxima and minima.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Eclipsed conformations are maxima; staggered conformations are minima.

facts.statement: Propane has a slightly larger rotational barrier than ethane because an eclipsed H/CH3 interaction is more costly than an eclipsed H/H interaction.
The propane rotational barrier is about 14 kJ/mol (3.4 kcal/mol).
An eclipsed H/CH3 interaction contributes about 6.0 kJ/mol (1.4 kcal/mol).
In butane, the anti conformation has the two methyl groups 180 degrees apart and is the lowest-energy staggered conformer.
In butane, a gauche conformation is staggered but places the two methyl groups 60 degrees apart; it is higher in energy than anti because of steric strain.
Steric strain is repulsion caused when atoms or groups are forced too close in space.
In butane, gauche is about 3.8 kJ/mol (0.9 kcal/mol) higher in energy than anti.
The eclipsed butane conformer with two CH3/H eclipsing interactions and one H/H eclipsing interaction is about 16 kJ/mol above anti.
The fully eclipsed butane conformer with CH3/CH3 eclipsing is about 19 kJ/mol above anti.
Larger alkanes are most stable when C-C bonds are staggered and large substituents are anti to one another where possible.
Room-temperature single-bond rotation means many conformers interconvert, but lower-energy conformers make up a larger fraction at any instant.

butane_rotation_profile.label: eclipsed
butane_rotation_profile.notes: Two CH3/H eclipsing interactions and one H/H eclipsing interaction.

butane_rotation_profile.label: gauche
butane_rotation_profile.notes: Methyl groups 60 degrees apart; local minimum.

butane_rotation_profile.label: fully eclipsed
butane_rotation_profile.notes: Methyl groups eclipse each other; highest-energy point.

candidate_cards.prompt: For propane, identify why the eclipsed conformer is higher in energy than the staggered conformer.
candidate_cards.answer: It contains eclipsing interactions, including one H/CH3 interaction, producing torsional strain.

candidate_cards.prompt: Classify a butane Newman projection as anti, gauche, or eclipsed.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Anti has CH3 groups 180 degrees apart; gauche has them 60 degrees apart; eclipsed has front and rear bonds aligned.

candidate_cards.prompt: Calculate the strain energy of an eclipsed butane conformer with two H/CH3 eclipsing interactions and one H/H eclipsing interaction.
Place anti, gauche, CH3/H eclipsed, and CH3/CH3 eclipsed butane conformations on an energy diagram.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Anti is the lowest minimum, gauche minima are at +3.8 kJ/mol, CH3/H eclipsed maxima are near +16 kJ/mol, and CH3/CH3 eclipsed is near +19 kJ/mol.

candidate_cards.prompt: Draw the most stable Newman projection along a specified bond of a substituted alkane.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Choose a staggered arrangement and place the largest substituents anti when possible.

candidate_cards.prompt: Draw the least stable Newman projection along a specified bond of a substituted alkane.
candidate_cards.answer_rule: Look for an eclipsed arrangement that places the largest substituents directly aligned.
